# Bash Gotchas

> Known bash shell patterns that cause silent failures or unexpected output. Load HIGH entries before writing any bash scripts.

## Entries

- [jq outputs pretty-printed JSON by default -- use -c for JSONL](jq-compact.md): jq -c produces single-line output. Without -c, grep and wc -l fail on multi-line JSON. HIGH.
- [Git Bash on Windows: PATH and tool availability](git-bash-windows.md): /usr/bin not always on PATH. Use explicit PATH setup or full paths for utilities in scripts and hooks. MEDIUM.
- [gh issue close --comment silently drops the comment on already-closed issues](gh-close-comment-on-already-closed.md): The --comment body is dropped (exit 0) when the issue is already closed. Comment-first, then close. MEDIUM.
- [Verify the current git branch before committing](verify-branch-before-commit.md): With shared working trees a parallel process can move HEAD; your next commit lands on the wrong branch and push says "Everything up-to-date". Check git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD first; push HEAD not a named ref. MEDIUM.
- [A PostToolUse hook that scans tool OUTPUT falsely records DB migrations](hook-scans-tool-output-false-record.md): psql echoes the migration filename in its error output, so a hook grepping the whole payload records failed applies and re-adds deleted rows. Scan tool_input.command only; skip on ERROR:/ROLLBACK. MEDIUM.
- [Fandom wikis: scrape via the MediaWiki API, not the HTML (Cloudflare blocks it)](fandom-mediawiki-api.md): Fandom article HTML sits behind a Cloudflare JS challenge that defeats WebFetch (403) and curl-with-browser-UA alike; use api.php (action=parse / action=query&prop=revisions / list=categorymembers) for raw wikitext instead. MEDIUM.
